description.value: A retrospective study used voxel-based morphometry and blinded visual assessment of MRI scans to identify regional gray matter atrophy patterns associated with pathologically defined frontotemporal dementia subgroups.

spans.text: We undertook this study to evaluate retrospectively the potential of brain MRI to predict specific pathologic substrates of FTD

description.value: Retrospective case study of pathologically confirmed frontotemporal dementia cases and age- and sex-matched healthy controls.

Masking procedures were used to identify regions of gray matter atrophy that were common to all pathologic subgroups and regions that were unique to each subgroup; these procedures applied Boolean criteria to every voxel in the thresholded statistical parametric map for each contrast.

An optimized method of VBM was used.17 Brain MRI studies from 10 healthy controls and 10 patients with a neurodegenerative disease (5 with FTD and 5 with Alzheimer disease), age and sex matched to the study cohort and acquired on the same scanner, were normalized to the Montreal Neurologic Institute standard brain.18 The mean template image was smoothed with an isotropic gaussian kernel of 8 mm full width at half maximum.

model_settings.value: Optimized voxel-based morphometry using SPM99 and MATLAB 6; images normalized to a customized Montreal Neurologic Institute template, segmented into gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid, masked to exclude nonbrain voxels, modulated, and smoothed with an 8-mm isotropic Gaussian kernel. The model included age, sex, and MMSE score as covariates. Inclusive and exclusive masking were used for subgroup contrasts.
